title: When maintenance runs into exercise time
summary: Decide what to reschedule when a repair takes longer than expected.

sections.heading: Fictional scenario
sections.body: Mara has a movement session followed by a rest break. A pump repair runs late and the next crew member is available to take over. The schedule still lists both breaks as completed.

sections.heading: Your turn
sections.body: Which parts of the schedule need correcting? What evidence would you need before changing the exercise plan?

sections.heading: One possible response
sections.body: Mark the movement session and rest break as missed. Ask when the relief worker can take over and look for room to restore both activities. Record the actual times so the next planner can see what happened.

sections.heading: Evidence and limits
sections.body: Jones reviewed indirect evidence suggesting that gravity at the Martian surface may provide too little loading to maintain conditioning over a long stay. The paper had no long-term human observations on Mars. It cannot tell Mara how long to exercise after this repair.

claims.text: Jones reviewed indirect evidence suggesting that gravity at the Martian surface may provide too little loading to maintain conditioning over a long stay.

sources.title: The Partial Gravity of the Moon and Mars Appears Insufficient to Maintain Human Health
